messages:
arjun: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression in the canary after we enabled multi-variant routing changes earlier today. p95 token-latency up ~12%, overall throughput down ~8% for a subset of routes.

maya: Can you paste the profiler outputs / logs you saw? which models and routes are affected?

arjun: Mostly routes hitting redwood-3b-quant + open-7b-compat variants. Quick paste from the runtime profiler (trimmed):

```
time window: 2026-03-16T21:40:00Z - 21:50:00Z
batches_total: 128K
avg_batch_size: 3.2
avg_batch_size[compat=A]: 5.8
avg_batch_size[compat=B]: 1.3
avg_batch_size[compat=C]: 1.1
kernel_selection: 73% triton_gemm_fp16, 22% amx_qkv8, 5% fallback_cpu
kv_cache_hit_rate: overall 87% but for compat B,C -> 61%
queue_wait_ms_p50: 2.1ms, p95: 9.7ms
per-token latency p95: 85ms -> 95ms after change
```

arjun: The thing that stands out is compat set fragmentation: many requests routed to variants that are "compatible" but differ in kernel profile, so the coalescer refuses to batch them faster and we get lots of tiny batches. Also KV miss for fallback-variants causing extra latency.

liam: Yep that matches my local repro. When compat diversity increases, the batching coalescer effectively serializes because it won't mix different kernel-affinity variants. Result is small batches + more kernel switches.

rebecca: Did you check token-budget shaping? If many requests have short prefix tokens, letting them wait for a slice to fill might help. Any breakdown by request length?

arjun: Good point — here's token-length distribution from the same window: 0-16 tokens: 58%, 17-64: 31%, 65+: 11%. So majority are short. With compat fragmentation, short requests are not aggregated.

jorge: Two angles: 1) change queue policy to allow cross-compat batching when token budgets are tiny (e.g., if expected batch size <4 and token budget <16, permit mixing variants and do a light-weight kernel adaptation path), or 2) introduce a compat-bucket-wait heuristic: for sparse compat buckets (<4 reqs) wait up to X ms before fallback to cross-compat merging.

maya: For (1) we need to verify kernel correctness when mixing variants. There are fast paths that depend on KV layout and attention kernels. We can add a permissive merge flag that only gets enabled if models share identical kv-layout/version + compatible quantization. That would avoid correctness issues.

ops-bot: Deploy note: any runtime change will require a canary across dedicated pools to catch KV warmup regressions. Suggest default canary 5% traffic, monitor kv_cache_miss_rate, per-route p95 token latency, kernel-switch-rate.

liam: I prototyped a small change: permissive_merge=true when (expected_batch_size_after_merge >=3 OR token_budget<=12) AND kv_layout_hash match. Local bench on 3k reqs: avg_batch_size improved 3.2 -> 4.9 for fragmented workload, p95 token latency dropped 95ms -> 78ms, kernel-switch-rate down 28%. No correctness failures in unit tests.

rebecca: Sounds promising. Can you add metrics for kv_cache_miss delta and model-specific fallback invocations? We saw an odd regression earlier where permissive merges increased kv thrash because fallback variants had different cache addressing.

liam: Added instrumentation in my branch: kv_miss_by_variant, cache_eviction_rate, fallback_invocations. In my runs kv_miss_by_variant for fallback variants stayed flat (+1%), eviction_rate slightly up (+0.6%) — within noise.

arjun: Proposed rollout plan:
- Stage 1: enable permissive_merge=false by default but expose permissive_merge=true via per-route canary flag.
- Stage 2: 5% traffic to canary for 2h, monitor p95, avg_batch_size, kv_miss_by_variant, kernel_switch_rate.
- Stage 3: if no regressions, increase canary to 25% and run overnight.

maya: Add unit-level kernel validation test (end-to-end with kv cache warmup) before any prod canary. Also add a guard: if kv_miss_by_variant increases >5% absolute in first 30m, auto rollback.

ops-bot: Canary checklist created: /ops/canaries/1880001234-permissive-merge. Health metrics: per-route p95, kv_miss_by_variant, kernel_switch_rate, avg_batch_size, tokens/sec. Auto-rollback thresholds noted.

rebecca: sgtm. Also let's try a small tweak to compat scoring: prefer variants with same kernel family during routing when the model has high short-token workload. That reduces fragmentation upstream.

arjun: Agree. I'll add a routing hint patch that penalizes kernel-family mismatches by +0.05 score for routes with >50% short-token traffic.

liam: I'll cut the perf branch and tests tonight, ping when ready for review.

maya: Thanks all — this thread captures the plan. Please paste canary links and perf dashboards when you have them. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Canary started at 2026-03-16T23:10:00Z for redwood-3b-quant on 5% traffic. Monitor: https://console.internal/canaries/1880001234
